master_measurements.desc: Total number of pixels the colony occupies.
master_measurements.name: Size_Area

master_measurements.desc: The sum of the object's grayscale pixel values.
master_measurements.name: Size_IntegratedIntensity

master_measurements.desc: Total length of the colony's outer boundary in pixels. Measures colony edge complexity and surface irregularity. Smooth, circular colonies have shorter perimeters relative to their area compared to irregular or filamentous colonies. Pixel perimeters read slightly high for round colonies (about 5% at radii above 80 px).
master_measurements.name: Size_Perimeter

master_measurements.desc: Area of the smallest convex polygon that completely contains the colony, computed from the convex hull of its pixel centers. Represents the colony's "filled-in" appearance if all indentations and holes were removed. Because the hull passes through pixel centers it is slightly smaller than the pixel count of a convex colony. Useful for detecting colony spreading patterns or invasive growth characteristics.
master_measurements.name: Size_ConvexArea

master_measurements.desc: Area of the smallest rectangle that completely contains the colony. Represents the total spatial shape of the colony including any empty space. In high-throughput assays, this helps assess colony positioning and potential interference with neighboring colonies.
master_measurements.name: Size_BboxArea

master_measurements.desc: Length of the longest axis of the ellipse that best fits the colony shape. Represents the maximum colony dimension. In arrayed microbial growth, this measurement helps identify colonies that have grown beyond their intended grid positions.
master_measurements.name: Size_MajorAxisLength

master_measurements.desc: Length of the shortest axis of the ellipse that best fits the colony shape. Represents the minimum colony dimension. Together with major axis length, this helps characterize colony aspect ratio and growth anisotropy.
master_measurements.name: Size_MinorAxisLength

master_measurements.desc: Minimum caliper diameter - the shortest distance between two parallel tangent lines touching opposite sides of the colony. Represents the narrowest dimension of the colony regardless of orientation. Useful for detecting elongated or irregular colony morphologies and measuring colony width.
master_measurements.name: Size_MinFeretDiameter

master_measurements.desc: Maximum caliper diameter - the longest distance between two parallel tangent lines touching opposite sides of the colony. Represents the maximum dimension of the colony regardless of orientation. Often exceeds major axis length for irregular shapes and helps quantify maximum colony extent.
master_measurements.name: Size_MaxFeretDiameter

master_measurements.desc: Radius of the largest circle that fits entirely inside the colony, equal to the maximum of the colony's Euclidean distance transform: the distance from the colony's deepest interior point to its nearest edge. For an ideal disk it equals the disk radius. It reflects the colony's narrowest dimension, not its overall extent: an elongated colony reports half its width whatever its length (a 100 x 20 pixel colony reports 10), and a runner or spur leaves it unchanged. Use MaxRadius for overall extent. The image border counts as an edge.
master_measurements.name: Size_InscribedRadius

master_measurements.desc: Median distance from the colony center to its boundary over the radial signature: the boundary distance sampled in equal angular directions (360 by default), keeping the outermost boundary crossing in each. The outer outline of every piece of the colony is sampled and holes are ignored, so a colony made of several pieces (a runner joined only at a corner, or fragments merged into one colony) is measured whole, and MaxRadius reaches its farthest piece. The center is the centroid of the distance-transform peak plateau; it lies inside compact colonies, but for a ring-shaped colony it can fall in the central hole. For an ideal disk it equals the disk radius; for an ideal 100 x 20 pixel rectangle it is 14.1 pixels. This is not the value the retired Shape_MedianRadius carried (a median distance to the nearest edge, now Shape_MedianBoundaryDist).
master_measurements.name: Size_MedianRadius

master_measurements.desc: Mean distance from the colony center to its boundary over the radial signature (see MedianRadius for the center and sampling). For an ideal disk it equals the disk radius; for an ideal 100 x 20 pixel rectangle it is 21.0 pixels. A runner or spur pulls it upward in proportion to its angular width; use RobustMeanRadius for the compact body. This is not the value the retired Shape_MeanRadius carried (a mean distance to the nearest edge, now Shape_MeanBoundaryDist).
master_measurements.name: Size_MeanRadius

master_measurements.desc: Symmetrically trimmed mean (20% from each end by default) of the radial signature (see MedianRadius). Because the signature is sampled by angle, a narrow runner contributes only its angular width and is trimmed away, so this estimates the typical radius of the colony's compact body. The trim treats genuine elongation the same way: an ideal 100 x 20 pixel rectangle gives 16.2 pixels against a MeanRadius of 21.0 pixels. For an ideal disk it equals the disk radius.
master_measurements.name: Size_RobustMeanRadius

master_measurements.desc: Largest distance from the colony center to its boundary over the radial signature (see MedianRadius): the colony's furthest reach. For an ideal disk it equals the disk radius; for an ideal 100 x 20 pixel rectangle it is 50.9 pixels. A MaxRadius far above RobustMeanRadius indicates a protrusion, spur, or runner. This is not the value the retired Shape_MaxRadius carried (the inscribed radius, now Size_InscribedRadius).
master_measurements.name: Size_MaxRadius

master_measurements.desc: Name of the image, which is the file name without its extension when the image is read from a file.
master_measurements.name: Metadata_ImageName

master_measurements.desc: Kind of image the row was measured from: Image, GridImage, Crop, Object or GridSection.
master_measurements.name: Metadata_ImageType

master_measurements.desc: Bit depth of the image's source pixel data, 8 or 16, either given when the image is loaded or inferred from the pixel data (16 for a float array).
master_measurements.name: Metadata_BitDepth

master_measurements.desc: The file suffix of the original file the image was imported from
master_measurements.name: Metadata_FileSuffix

master_measurements.desc: Integer label uniquely identifying each detected object (colony) within its source image. Acts as the per-image primary key shared by every measurement table, letting all per-colony measurements be joined together and traced back to a single colony on the agar plate.
master_measurements.name: Object_Label

master_measurements.desc: Row coordinate of the colony's centroid, the mean position of its pixels (skimage ``centroid``).
master_measurements.name: Bbox_CenterRR

master_measurements.desc: Column coordinate of the colony's centroid, the mean position of its pixels (skimage ``centroid``).
master_measurements.name: Bbox_CenterCC

master_measurements.desc: The smallest row coordinate of the bounding box.
master_measurements.name: Bbox_MinRR

master_measurements.desc: The smallest column coordinate of the bounding box.
master_measurements.name: Bbox_MinCC

master_measurements.desc: The largest row coordinate of the bounding box. It is one past the colony's last pixel row (exclusive, as in Python slicing), so rows MinRR to MaxRR - 1 hold the colony and ``image[MinRR:MaxRR]`` covers it.
master_measurements.name: Bbox_MaxRR

master_measurements.desc: The largest column coordinate of the bounding box. It is one past the colony's last pixel column (exclusive, as in Python slicing), so columns MinCC to MaxCC - 1 hold the colony and ``image[:, MinCC:MaxCC]`` covers it.
master_measurements.name: Bbox_MaxCC

master_measurements.desc: The intensity-weighted center row coordinate of the object (skimage ``centroid_weighted``).
master_measurements.name: Bbox_IntensityWeightedCenterRR

master_measurements.desc: The intensity-weighted center column coordinate of the object (skimage ``centroid_weighted``).
master_measurements.name: Bbox_IntensityWeightedCenterCC

master_measurements.desc: Row coordinate of the colony's distance-weighted centroid: the mean position of its pixels, each weighted by its distance to the colony's edge. It is Σ dt·row / Σ dt over the Euclidean distance transform dt, and the plain centroid for a colony whose every pixel has a pixel of another colony among its eight neighbors (those pixels are zeroed before the transform, so its weights sum to 0). Robust to thin filamentous extensions that pull intensity-weighted centroids off-body.
master_measurements.name: Bbox_DistWeightedCenterRR

master_measurements.desc: Column coordinate of the colony's distance-weighted centroid: the mean position of its pixels, each weighted by its distance to the colony's edge. It is Σ dt·col / Σ dt over the Euclidean distance transform dt, and the plain centroid for a colony whose every pixel has a pixel of another colony among its eight neighbors (those pixels are zeroed before the transform, so its weights sum to 0). Robust to thin filamentous extensions that pull intensity-weighted centroids off-body.
master_measurements.name: Bbox_DistWeightedCenterCC

master_measurements.desc: Zero-based row number, from 0 at the top, of the grid cell that holds the colony's centroid (the mean position of its pixels). A colony whose centroid lies outside the grid is assigned to the nearest edge row.
master_measurements.name: Grid_RowNum

master_measurements.desc: Zero-based column number, from 0 at the left, of the grid cell that holds the colony's centroid (the mean position of its pixels). A colony whose centroid lies outside the grid is assigned to the nearest edge column.
master_measurements.name: Grid_ColNum

master_measurements.desc: Zero-based number of the colony's grid cell, counted left to right along each row and then down the rows. It is RowNum × (number of grid columns) + ColNum. Row major is the standard in most programming and data science array libraries. Used for indexing into 2D arrays.
master_measurements.name: Grid_RowMajorIdx

master_measurements.desc: Zero-based number of the colony's grid cell, counted top to bottom down each column and then across the columns. It is ColNum × (number of grid rows) + RowNum. Lab automation logic uses column-major (column-wise) indexing for well plate operations because 96-well plates are physically arranged with 8 rows (labeled A-H) and 12 columns (numbered 1-12), and this layout maps directly to how multichannel pipettes operate.
master_measurements.name: Grid_ColMajorIdx

master_measurements.desc: Dataset name used to group CLI-emitted measurements.
master_measurements.name: Metadata_Dataset

measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.desc: Zero-based number of the colony's grid cell, counted top to bottom down each column and then across the columns. It is ColNum × (number of grid rows) + RowNum. Lab automation logic uses column-major (column-wise) indexing for well plate operations because 96-well plates are physically arranged with 8 rows (labeled A-H) and 12 columns (numbered 1-12), and this layout maps directly to how multichannel pipettes operate.
measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.name: Grid_ColMajorIdx

measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.desc: Total number of pixels the colony occupies.
measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.name: Size_Area

measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.desc: The sum of the object's grayscale pixel values.
measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.name: Size_IntegratedIntensity

measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.desc: Total length of the colony's outer boundary in pixels. Measures colony edge complexity and surface irregularity. Smooth, circular colonies have shorter perimeters relative to their area compared to irregular or filamentous colonies. Pixel perimeters read slightly high for round colonies (about 5% at radii above 80 px).
measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.name: Size_Perimeter

measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.desc: Area of the smallest convex polygon that completely contains the colony, computed from the convex hull of its pixel centers. Represents the colony's "filled-in" appearance if all indentations and holes were removed. Because the hull passes through pixel centers it is slightly smaller than the pixel count of a convex colony. Useful for detecting colony spreading patterns or invasive growth characteristics.
measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.name: Size_ConvexArea

measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.desc: Area of the smallest rectangle that completely contains the colony. Represents the total spatial shape of the colony including any empty space. In high-throughput assays, this helps assess colony positioning and potential interference with neighboring colonies.
measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.name: Size_BboxArea

measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.desc: Length of the longest axis of the ellipse that best fits the colony shape. Represents the maximum colony dimension. In arrayed microbial growth, this measurement helps identify colonies that have grown beyond their intended grid positions.
measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.name: Size_MajorAxisLength

measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.desc: Length of the shortest axis of the ellipse that best fits the colony shape. Represents the minimum colony dimension. Together with major axis length, this helps characterize colony aspect ratio and growth anisotropy.
measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.name: Size_MinorAxisLength

measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.desc: Minimum caliper diameter - the shortest distance between two parallel tangent lines touching opposite sides of the colony. Represents the narrowest dimension of the colony regardless of orientation. Useful for detecting elongated or irregular colony morphologies and measuring colony width.
measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.name: Size_MinFeretDiameter

measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.desc: Maximum caliper diameter - the longest distance between two parallel tangent lines touching opposite sides of the colony. Represents the maximum dimension of the colony regardless of orientation. Often exceeds major axis length for irregular shapes and helps quantify maximum colony extent.
measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.name: Size_MaxFeretDiameter

measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.desc: Radius of the largest circle that fits entirely inside the colony, equal to the maximum of the colony's Euclidean distance transform: the distance from the colony's deepest interior point to its nearest edge. For an ideal disk it equals the disk radius. It reflects the colony's narrowest dimension, not its overall extent: an elongated colony reports half its width whatever its length (a 100 x 20 pixel colony reports 10), and a runner or spur leaves it unchanged. Use MaxRadius for overall extent. The image border counts as an edge.
measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.name: Size_InscribedRadius

measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.desc: Median distance from the colony center to its boundary over the radial signature: the boundary distance sampled in equal angular directions (360 by default), keeping the outermost boundary crossing in each. The outer outline of every piece of the colony is sampled and holes are ignored, so a colony made of several pieces (a runner joined only at a corner, or fragments merged into one colony) is measured whole, and MaxRadius reaches its farthest piece. The center is the centroid of the distance-transform peak plateau; it lies inside compact colonies, but for a ring-shaped colony it can fall in the central hole. For an ideal disk it equals the disk radius; for an ideal 100 x 20 pixel rectangle it is 14.1 pixels. This is not the value the retired Shape_MedianRadius carried (a median distance to the nearest edge, now Shape_MedianBoundaryDist).
measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.name: Size_MedianRadius

measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.desc: Mean distance from the colony center to its boundary over the radial signature (see MedianRadius for the center and sampling). For an ideal disk it equals the disk radius; for an ideal 100 x 20 pixel rectangle it is 21.0 pixels. A runner or spur pulls it upward in proportion to its angular width; use RobustMeanRadius for the compact body. This is not the value the retired Shape_MeanRadius carried (a mean distance to the nearest edge, now Shape_MeanBoundaryDist).
measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.name: Size_MeanRadius

measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.desc: Symmetrically trimmed mean (20% from each end by default) of the radial signature (see MedianRadius). Because the signature is sampled by angle, a narrow runner contributes only its angular width and is trimmed away, so this estimates the typical radius of the colony's compact body. The trim treats genuine elongation the same way: an ideal 100 x 20 pixel rectangle gives 16.2 pixels against a MeanRadius of 21.0 pixels. For an ideal disk it equals the disk radius.
measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.name: Size_RobustMeanRadius

measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.desc: Largest distance from the colony center to its boundary over the radial signature (see MedianRadius): the colony's furthest reach. For an ideal disk it equals the disk radius; for an ideal 100 x 20 pixel rectangle it is 50.9 pixels. A MaxRadius far above RobustMeanRadius indicates a protrusion, spur, or runner. This is not the value the retired Shape_MaxRadius carried (the inscribed radius, now Size_InscribedRadius).
measurements_by_feature/MeasureSize.name: Size_MaxRadius
